title: Convoy PQ 17
subtitle: Arctic · 27 June – 13 July 1942
footnote: British Double Summer Time (UTC+2). Merchant-ship sinking positions from uboat.net and Wikipedia's shipwreck lists (three positions are unrecorded and are placed by their groups; two published latitudes look like misprints and are noted); the convoy's track between sightings, the cruisers' and Home Fleet's movements and Tirpitz's sortie are reconstructed. US and Panamanian ships are counted as US losses, British, Dutch and Soviet as British. Formation members are spread slightly so they don't overlap.

convoy.name: Commodore John Dowding RNR
convoy.bio: Watched his convoy ordered apart at 21:36 on 4 July — 'the scatter signal was a bitter pill' — was sunk with his own ship the next night, rescued by Lotus, and then spent a fortnight gathering the survivors out of Novaya Zemlya's bays and bringing them into Archangel.
convoy.fate: Survived; commodore of later Russian convoys.

escort.name: Commander Jack Broome
escort.bio: Read the three Admiralty signals as meaning Tirpitz was over the horizon, scattered the convoy and took his destroyers to reinforce the cruisers — the decision he defended for the rest of his life, and won a libel action over.
escort.fate: Captain; wrote Convoy Is To Scatter; died 1985.

cs1.name: Rear-Admiral Louis Hamilton
cs1.bio: Kept his four cruisers with the convoy beyond his orders, then obeyed 'withdraw to the westward at high speed' at 22:30 — taking Broome's destroyers with him and leaving the merchantmen to the aircraft and U-boats.

homefleet.name: Admiral Sir John Tovey
homefleet.bio: Had argued against running PQ 17 in the perpetual daylight of July and been overruled. Held the battlefleet and Victorious west of Bear Island as the bait for Tirpitz, too far to help the convoy — 'the most dreadful thing'.

tirpitz.name: Generaladmiral Otto Schniewind
tirpitz.bio: Sailed on his own authority at 11:00 on 5 July before Hitler's permission came, was recalled at 21:30 without firing a shot — and won the battle anyway: the mere threat had scattered the convoy.

kummetz.name: Vizeadmiral Oskar Kummetz
kummetz.bio: Lost his flagship to a rock in the Tjeldsund before the operation began. Six months later he would fight the Barents Sea action against JW 51B.

k21.name: Captain 2nd Rank Nikolai Lunin
k21.bio: Fired four stern torpedoes at Tirpitz off Ingøy at 17:00 on 5 July and reported two hits. German records show none, but the Soviet Union celebrated the attack for decades.
k21.fate: Hero of the Soviet Union; rear-admiral; died 1970.

u255.name: Kapitänleutnant Reinhart Reche
u255.bio: Made the first contact east of Jan Mayen on 1 July and sank four ships — John Witherspoon, Alcoa Ranger, Olopana and, eight days after the scatter, the derelict Paulus Potter, whose confidential books he boarded her to take.
u255.fate: Knight's Cross; survived the war; died 1993.

strikes.name: BV 138 shadowers
strikes.note: From 1 July the convoy is never out of sight of a flying boat

strikes.name: He 115 floatplanes — first attack
strikes.note: 1./KüFlGr 906: seven torpedo floatplanes, no hits; one shot down and its crew rescued by another He 115

strikes.name: Lone He 115 in the fog
strikes.note: A single torpedo out of the fog stops Christopher Newport — the first loss

strikes.name: I./KG 26 — 25 He 111 torpedo bombers
strikes.note: Hauptmann Eicke's Heinkels come in at mast height through Wainwright's barrage: Navarino and William Hooper sunk, Azerbaidjan hit; four aircraft lost. Two hours later the convoy is ordered to scatter

strikes.name: KG 30 Ju 88s — 5 July
strikes.note: With the convoy scattered and its escort gone, Bloedorn's Ju 88s pick off ships singly all afternoon: Washington, Bolton Castle, Paulus Potter, Pan Kraft, Fairfield City, Peter Kerr, Zaafaran; Earlston, Empire Byron, Aldersdale and Daniel Morgan crippled for the U-boats

strikes.name: II./KG 30 off the Murman coast
strikes.note: The Matochkin group, within 60 miles of the Kola coast: Hoosier and El Capitan stopped, Samuel Chase damaged

strikes.name: Catalina finds Tirpitz
strikes.note: A 210 Squadron Catalina from Grasnaya reports the battle group off the North Cape — an hour after Raeder has already decided to recall it

torpedoes.note: The Soviet tanker's linseed oil blows sky-high — and she steams on
Coup de grâce after P614's torpedo fails
Dowding, his commodore's staff and the survivors are picked up by Lotus
38 of her crew die in the water
Reche's boarding party takes her confidential books first
Four stern torpedoes at 4,000 m; two explosions heard — the Germans notice nothing

engagements.note: Wainwright charges the Heinkels head-on; the AA ships and every merchantman's Oerlikons open up
Merchant gunners alone; Daniel Morgan claims two Ju 88s
Deck gun on the abandoned Alcoa Ranger
